subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — GPU sizing & SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity performance validation — next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and clear signal that Acme AI's inference needs are latency-sensitive for user-facing features. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps for the dedicated validation run: 

Recap / Requirements (from call)
- 99th percentile tail latency target: <= 120 ms for single-turn chat generation at typical prompt length (~120 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: ~150 reqs/min (peak bursts to 300 reqs/min).
- Concurrency requirement: support 40 concurrent real-time sessions with streaming responses.
- Streaming: server-side streaming required (token-by-token), client expects latency to first token < 80 ms.
- Model: planning to run the open-weights LlamaX-70B quantized variant.

Proposed validation plan
1) Baseline bench on A100-80GB and RTX A6000 to compare steady-state throughput and 99p latency.
2) Run reserved throughput sizing with continuous batching profiles that match your traffic shape (we'll use the trace you shared).
3) Validate streaming token latency and first-token requirement.
4) Provide final SLO sizing recommendation and a mutual action plan (MAP) for Dedicated.

Attachments: I attached a short GPU comparison and a draft MAP that outlines deliverables and timeline.

Can you confirm the latency/throughput targets above and the model variant? Once confirmed, Aditya will propose a concrete sizing and schedule the validation run for next week.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: gpu-comparison-RTXA6000-v-A100.pdf] [Attachment: mutual-action-plan-acme-ai.docx]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@cloudinfra.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity performance validation — next steps

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that's exactly what we discussed. Confirming the key targets from our end:
- 99p <= 120 ms (critical)
- Sustained 150 reqs/min, burst 300 reqs/min
- 40 concurrent streaming sessions, first-token < 80 ms
- Model: LlamaX-70B quantized (we're using 4-bit quant + KV cache)

A couple of clarifying questions before you schedule the run:
1) In the streaming scenario, how do you account for per-session KV cache sizing? We need to understand GPU memory pressure with 40 concurrent sessions.
2) For the reserved throughput runs, can you show both single-GPU and 2x-GPU configurations (A100 vs A6000) so we can evaluate cost vs performance?
3) Any recommended fallbacks (smaller model flavor or reduced context) if tail latency spikes during peak?

Priya (our infra lead) is CC'd — she will provide the traffic trace and token distribution we discussed.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platform | Acme AI
alex.johnson@acme.ai
[External: please attach any benchmarking notes as CSVs]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@cloudinfra.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity performance validation — next steps

Alex / Priya —

Thanks — this is doable. Quick engineering read on the three asks:

1) KV cache memory: For LlamaX-70B at 4-bit quant, per-token KV size is ~0.45 KB (after quantization + packing). For 40 concurrent sessions with average context window of 1024 tokens, that implies ~18 MB of KV per session (approx). Total KV ~720 MB, plus model parameter memory. On an A100-80GB we have comfortable headroom for model + KV for single-GPU runs; RTX A6000 (48GB) will be tight for single-GPU at full concurrency — we'd need a 2x-A6000 configuration or use model sharding.

2) GPU comparison: We'll run bench matrix: A100-80GB (single GPU), A100-80GB (2x), A6000 (2x). We'll capture: avg latency, 95p, 99p, first-token latency, throughput at target concurrency, and memory headroom. See attached initial comparison doc.

3) Fallbacks / SLO controls:
- Canary model flavor: LlamaX-30B quantized as fallback (50% lower memory/throughput needs).
- Dynamic batching caps and admission control to preserve 99p SLO (we can set per-route concurrency limits).
- Streaming optimization: start-of-stream fast-path to reduce first-token latency (we can enable KV-prefetch for hot sessions).

Proposed next steps:
- Priya: please share the trace (token distribution + QPS over 24h) — that'll let us generate a realistic batching profile.
- Once we have the trace, schedule 8-hour validation window: 2 hours per config to warm + 1 hour for steady-state capture.
- We'll deliver a CSV with raw samples (attached) and a final sizing recommendation.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-run-11-28.csv (sample benchmark), gpu-comparison-RTXA6000-v-A100.pdf

I'll aim to have a proposed slot for next Wed/Thu.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Aditya — super helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups inline:

> For 40 concurrent sessions with average context window of 1024 tokens, that implies ~18 MB of KV per session (approx).

Does that number assume attention cache per layer kept on GPU? We have some local tooling that offloads older KV pages after N tokens; would that be compatible with your runtime?

> Proposed next steps: Priya: please share the trace

Trace attached (see Priya's email thread). Also attaching a short doc on our expected client-side streaming semantics — we need heartbeat-friendly partial tokens every ~50 ms.

About scheduling: Wednesday next week (Dec 2) looks good for us; we can provide a pre-provisioned VPC endpoint if you want a private test.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex / Priya —

Great — thanks for the trace and the streaming notes. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) Scheduling: Marissa / Aditya to lock Dec 2 validation window (we'll provision A100-80GB single-GPU and 2x-A6000 configs).
2) Engineering runbook: Aditya + Rafael to own benchmark runs and produce CSV/plots.
3) Fallback plan: Rafael to prototype a LlamaX-30B canary config for admission control testing.
4) Security & network: Dev to coordinate VPC endpoint access for the test.
4) Delivery: final sizing recommendation and MAP update by Dec 4.

I've attached the MAP with milestones and the sample CSV from Aditya. Please confirm acceptance of the MAP and call out any blockers. If nobody objects, we'll schedule the run first thing Wednesday and send a calendar invite.
